title: About
introText: I work on QA and test automation for Pega applications, in the Sopra Steria Pega Practice (RulesMatter). Most of my background is in financial services, where release discipline and audit trails are hard requirements. I hold Certified Pega Business Architect (CPBA) and Certified Pega System Architect (CPSA), and certified as a Tricentis Tosca Product Consultant at Advanced proficiency. Fluent in Dutch, English, and Turkish (native).
introQuote: What I care about most is reliability. I want a framework I build to still work three releases from now, not just on the day I commit it. When a test goes flaky I'd rather find out why (timing, state pollution, data dependency) than rerun it until it goes green.
storyPart1: Before Sopra Steria I spent two years at ING as a Test Automation Engineer on Dovetail, the Fiserv real-time international payments platform. I built and maintained the shared Selenium, Cucumber and Java framework behind the daily regression suites, covering incoming and outgoing payment flows across four countries. I studied Applied Mathematics at Istanbul University, and it shows up in how I approach coverage decisions, edge cases, and breaking scenarios into independent variables. I am also ISTQB Certified Tester Foundation Level (CTFL).
storyPart2: I think about what level a test should live at, since end-to-end coverage is expensive and a unit test doesn't always prove what people assume it proves. The Tosca certification path covers web, API, desktop and mobile automation, along with test data and stateful scenarios. The reason for combining it with Pega is to get testability into the case design from the start. I use AI-assisted coding tools daily (Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot) and build infrastructure around them: the Devran AI Kit is an open-source framework I maintain for governance, quality gates, and session-persistent context. The questions there are the same ones as in QA: what makes output trustworthy, and how do you make that trust auditable.
storyPart3: Through Sopra Steria I am available for QA Consultant, QA Lead, or Test Automation Engineer assignments in a Pega context, ideally where model-based automation in Tosca is the approach. My preference is financial services or government engagements. If this lines up with what you're working on, feel free to reach out. I'm always up for a conversation about testing real-time payment systems, model-based automation, or scaling QA inside a Pega project.

testAutomation.title: Test Automation Architecture
testAutomation.description: Building robust, scalable end-to-end automation frameworks to ensure software quality and reliability.
testAutomation.fullDescription: I specialize in designing and implementing enterprise-grade test automation frameworks that scale with your business. From UI testing with Selenium and Playwright to API validation with REST Assured, I build comprehensive solutions that catch bugs before they reach production. My frameworks follow clean architecture principles with Page Object Model, making them maintainable and easy for teams to adopt.

Catch critical bugs early with automated smoke and sanity tests
Scale QA coverage without proportionally scaling team size
Integrate seamlessly with CI/CD pipelines for continuous feedback
Maintainable frameworks following industry best practices

cicd.title: CI/CD & DevOps Integration
cicd.description: Designing and maintaining continuous integration pipelines to accelerate deployment and reduce risk.

My approach includes containerization with Docker, automated test execution, and comprehensive reporting.

apiBackend.title: API & Backend Validation

pegaPlatform.title: Pega Platform Architecture
pegaPlatform.description: Designing testable Pega applications from the case model up, certified as both Business Architect and System Architect.
pegaPlatform.fullDescription: Test automation on Pega stays fragile without understanding the platform from the inside, so the Certified Pega Business Architect and Certified Pega System Architect certifications came before the tooling. I work within the Sopra Steria Pega Practice (RulesMatter) on case design, data models, and the platform decisions that determine whether an application can be tested at all. Getting testability into the case design from the start is far cheaper than bolting it on after the fact.
keyBenefits: Case design and data modelling reviewed for testability from day one
Certified Pega Business Architect (CPBA): business rules and case lifecycle
Certified Pega System Architect (CPSA): data models, integrations, security
Bridges business analysts and QA with a shared platform vocabulary
Foundation for model-based automation in Tricentis Tosca

toscaAutomation.title: Tricentis Tosca Test Automation
toscaAutomation.description: Model-based test automation across web, API, desktop and mobile. Certified Product Consultant at Advanced proficiency.
toscaAutomation.fullDescription: I design test coverage, test data, and automation architecture using Tosca's model-based approach, scanning applications into reusable modules rather than writing brittle scripts. The Product Consultant certification came out of the full 13-course Tricentis Academy learning plan, roughly 63 hours of training, with the exam passed at 93.3%. The path covers web UI (AS1/AS2), API chains, automation beyond the browser through the Excel, PDF, Mail, UIA and WinX engines, requirements-driven TestCase design with risk weighting, stateful test data through the Test Data Service, and mobile automation on the Tricentis Mobile Agent. Combined with Pega platform knowledge, this lets testability be designed in rather than retrofitted.
keyBenefits: Model-based automation across web, desktop, API and mobile in one toolchain
Reusable TestStepBlocks, recovery scenarios and multi-browser execution
Stateful test data management across distributed test runs (TDS)
Risk-weighted, requirements-driven TestCase design
Mobile automation on the Tricentis Mobile Agent, including image-based cases
Product Consultant certification exam passed at 93.3%
